scientific_figures.relative_shared_rays.png: Schematic reference rays from two nearby sources to one station. The shaded region represents a broad velocity anomaly. The straight rays illustrate first-order common-path sensitivity.

relative_hayward_pair.png.description: The identical 16 earthquake IDs from the hypoDD example1 tables near El Cerrito. Both sections use one origin, azimuth 325°, identical axes and positive-down depths. The original location depths span 2.010 km, the relocated depths span 0.332 km.
relative_hayward_pair.png.reference: Waldhauser & Ellsworth (2000), https://doi.org/10.1785/0120000006. Example data from Felix Waldhauser’s hypoDD package, example1.

relative_dysa_triangle.png.source: Iceland100/reference/dt.cc; arrow tail time minus head time.

scientific_figures.relative_kver_waveforms.png: Iceland100, Z7.KVER, P, events 1 and 2. Julia export from teaching/source/export_kver.jl, plotted in units of each trace’s scaled amplitude.
scientific_figures.relative_kver_correlation.png: Same pair, station and phase as waveform figure. Julia symmetric finite-window correlation export. Highest sampled coefficient is 0.7998529 at +20 ms. DDCorr’s interpolated peak is +20.2 ms.
scientific_figures.relative_subsample.png: Illustrative continuous pulse sampled at integer times, and the same pulse delayed by one-tenth of a sample. Poupinet, Ellsworth & Fréchet (1984), https://doi.org/10.1029/JB089iB07p05719, reported time resolution about one order of magnitude finer than the digitization interval in their earthquake-doublet analysis.

reproduction: lecture_figures.py --repo PATH_TO_DDCORR --hayward EXAMPLE1_DIR --output ASSET_DIR. The two Hayward coordinate tables can be obtained at the pinned source links above.
